Bonjour,

Je m'appelle Mika, depuis toute petite je suis passionné par l'espace et mars fait partie d'un pôle majeur de cette passion, je suis vulgarisatrice scientifique et infographiste spécialisé dans le domaine spatial, je possède un diplôme de modélisation 3D ainsi que plusieurs certificats, notamment du Space app challenge 2025.
summary:
Mapping Jezero Crater: A Tool for Preparing Human Survival on Mars

As part of the "Survival on Mars" challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I developed a series of maps of Jezero Crater, located on the planet Mars.

My project provides several cartographic representations of the same region in different formats: colored and grayscale maps, terrain representations with and without relief, as well as maps highlighting strategic locations and potentially hazardous areas.

The main objective is to improve understanding of the Martian terrain and help identify important areas for exploration, navigation, and the planning of future missions.

By combining different representations of the terrain and geographical features of Jezero Crater, these maps provide a visualization and decision-support tool to help anticipate potential environmental challenges and contribute to the preparation of future human missions to Mars.

Ultimately, this project aims to make Martian geographical data more accessible, understandable, and useful for planning safer exploration of the Red Planet.
details: Strategic Mapping of Jezero Crater: Assessing Risks and Supporting Safe Navigation on Mars My project consists of creating a series of maps of Jezero Crater on Mars to facilitate terrain analysis and contribute to the preparation of future human exploration missions. The project offers several cartographic formats: colored and grayscale maps, terrain maps with and without relief, as well as visual representations highlighting strategic locations and potentially hazardous areas. The project works by observing and comparing different representations of the Martian surface. Its main objective is to help distinguish potentially dangerous areas from locations that appear safer for navigation. These maps can help identify terrain features, obstacles, and geographical characteristics that could make movement difficult for astronauts or exploration vehicles. One of the main advantages of this project is that it makes geographical information easier to understand and use. By providing several complementary types of maps, it allows users to examine the same region from different perspectives and identify potentially safer routes, areas to avoid, and locations of strategic interest. The expected impact is to contribute to improving the preparation and safety of future Mars exploration missions. A better understanding of the terrain could help mission teams anticipate potential hazards, plan movements, and make more informed decisions while exploring the Martian surface. The creativity of this project lies in combining several cartographic representations within a single visualization approach. Instead of providing just one map, it offers different ways to interpret the Martian landscape, making terrain analysis more accessible and comprehensive. The main factors considered include topography, elevation variations, geographical obstacles, potentially hazardous areas, navigation possibilities, and the strategic importance of certain locations within Jezero Crater. For its development, the project uses geographical maps and data of Mars, including topographic representations and images of the Martian surface. The tools and software used are those that made it possible to access, analyze, and create the different cartographic representations. This project is part of a broader effort to prepare for human exploration of Mars: understanding the terrain today to help make navigation safer tomorrow.
